messages:
tara-support: acme-corp reporting intermittent 502s and TCP resets to their Private endpoint since ~09:12 UTC after a peering change. Customer sees TLS handshake failures; API traffic drops. Can infra confirm any peering/route changes?
oncall-bot: [ALERT] private-endpoint-502 spike (service=private-api, region=eu-west-1) — incident created: INC-2248. Pager duty: @nathan-eng oncall.
acme-sysadmin: seeing tons of `TLS handshake error: remote error: handshake failure` in our app logs. No changes on our side besides a routine restart. We also see `connection reset by peer` from client side.
jeff-infra: thanks. Any recent cert rotations, BGP flaps, or IP changes on Redwood side? Also need a quick `traceroute` and `dig` from acme to verify path + DNS.
ben-ops: grabbed packet capture from peering link. snippet: ```17:20:13.123456 IP x.x.x.x.4500 > y.y.y.y.4500: UDP, length 64 - NAT-T ISAKMP/ESP``` and BGP neighbor shows: ```Neighbor 10.1.2.1 AS 65001 is established, prefixes received 0 (was 120)``` — looks like route suppression after rekey.
nathan-eng: possible NAT-T/UDP encapsulation problem + missing egress allowlist. For ExpressRoute/VPN peers we need UDP/500 and UDP/4500 allowed egress on customer firewall and also allow the peer IPs for control-plane (BGP). Also check that the CA bundle for the private control plane matches the customer peering config after cert rotation.
tara-support: acme, can you run `dig +short private-api.acme.internal` from a host that hits the private peering and paste output? Also curl -v to capture TLS failure.
acme-sysadmin: dig output: `10.240.5.12` (resolves to internal IP). Reverse lookup returns NXDOMAIN. curl -v result: ```* Connected to private-api.acme.internal (10.240.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: Received fatal alert: handshake_failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure```
jeff-infra: curl shows server sent handshake failure. That plus BGP prefix drop suggests our peering agent failed to advertise the correct VIP after the cert rotation; customers hit a fallback host that doesn't have the right cert (SNI mismatch). Can we confirm which cert is active on the peering pod?
nathan-eng: I rotated the intermediate yesterday — I forgot to push the updated CA bundle into the private control plane config for acme's VPC peering. Fix: push CA bundle and restart peering-agent on the dedicated tenant. Command sequence I will run: ```rdsctl peering update-ca --tenant acme-corp --ca-file /tmp/acme-ca.pem && kubectl -n peering rollout restart deploy/peering-agent-acme``` Expect small disruption but should restore correct cert chain and BGP advertisements.
ben-ops: pushed bundle and restarted agent at 09:34 UTC. Agent logs: `peering-agent-acme: loaded CA bundle, BGP adj restored, advertised 120 prefixes` — initial verification shows prefixes back and no NAT-T errors.
tara-support: acme can you re-run curl -v / quick smoke? Also confirm latency/502 metrics.
acme-sysadmin: reran at 09:36 UTC: TLS handshake now completes, HTTP 200 responses returning. No more resets. Thanks, team.
oncall-bot: [RESOLVED] INC-2248 — private-endpoint-502 spike resolved (root cause: missing CA bundle after cert rotation affecting peering agent; fix deployed).
